justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: No RCTs supporting visceral manipulation for any condition. Case reports and small studies dominate.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Multiple 5-day modules; years to complete full pathway; very high cumulative time and cost.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to chronic pain and visceral dysfunction; very limited evidence base restricts clinical acceptance.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: No third-party coverage; self-pay only; no insurance billing pathway.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Minimal employer demand; primarily private practice with specific manual therapy focus.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Some patients report benefit, consistent with non-specific and placebo effects.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Visceral manipulation is a quintessential cash-pay manual therapy niche with motivated self-pay clientele.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Practitioners routinely charge $200-300+/hr out of network.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Rare, distinctive brand; strong differentiation in a manual therapy market.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Highly personality- and hands-driven; very hard to scale beyond the owner-clinician.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Niche but devoted consumer following, especially in wellness-oriented markets.
justifications.business.efficiency: Long, expensive multi-course pathway with international seminars.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Viewed skeptically by academic PT; commercial brand with no ABPTRFE standing.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Limited curricular fit; not part of standard DPT manual therapy content.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Evidence base is weak and contested.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Essentially never preferred in faculty hiring.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Expensive and slow for negligible academic payoff.
